title: The Bow Hero's First Lesson
text: “Now then… I know you’re hiding somewhere, so please come out.”
“Tch! Ruined the whole setup—what a boring turn of events, nano. Nano, nano!”
Rival, who was standing beside me, clicked her tongue, I say.
“Itsuki… you didn’t have to crush the flag like that…”
Father protested to Itsuki at this point, I say.
“So you really were hiding… I’d guess it was going to be something like ‘I show up out of nowhere with no foreshadowing right when I’m in a pinch,’ or something along those lines.”
“Wouldn’t that role be more suited to Rafumi-chan, if anything? I was thinking more along the lines of the classic school-story cliché myself.”
“It’s fine either way. I don’t need that kind of cliché. Honestly… so this is why Gaelion-san was pushing this so hard for no reason.”
“Itsuki… you really ought to honor the classics, I say. Pig though it may be.”
This sort of commotion was daily fare for me, I say! Not that I, being a pig, had any desire to partake in it, I say!
“Would you please stop teasing me about the whole Rafuemon-san business already, Gaelion-san!”
“Gaelion wasn’t steering anything, nano.”
“Itsuki, isn’t that rather rude to Rafuemon…”
“Of all the excuses, ‘I wasn’t steering anything’ is a rather exasperating one to hear.”
“It’s a fact that this world’s Naofumi had nothing to do with it, nano. It was only recommended because Wild Naofumi said it was well-suited for the Bow Hero, nano.”
“So the Naofumi-san from another world is the true culprit…”

“Well… I mean, given Itsuki’s background and all, it does seem like the kind of event that was bound to happen, so I get why it was tailored for him. Are you maybe a little happy about it, deep down?”
“Please be quiet. If anything, isn’t this sort of thing more Motoyasu-san’s specialty? Ignoring the pig business, of course.”
“Indeed, I’ve had my fair share of experience with it, I say.”

For some reason, back at the dorm, in what was supposedly my room, a pig had gone and used the shower fixtures without permission, I say. What Itsuki did was entirely correct, I say. Severe punishment is due for any pig who uses someone’s room without leave, I say.

“A girl who bites into a slice of bread on her first day transferring schools… and probably collides with someone—maybe a pig—at a corner at some point. That sounds like something that’d happen to you, Motoyasu-kun.”
Father’s words jogged my memory, I say. Hmm…
“It has happened a few times, I say. Though the transfer-day incident only occurred once. On other occasions, I have collided with pigs while making their acquaintance, I say.”
Colliding at street corners was indeed a recurring theme, I say.
“Sounds like a case tailor-made for both Motoyasu-kun and Itsuki, then~ If Itsuki had just won his duels properly, maybe he could’ve had a nice school life with that girl, you know?”
“Honestly, the whole ‘if something displeases you, challenge them to a duel’ flow strikes me as nothing short of barbaric. I’ll pass on that sort of person, thank you.”

Ugh! Itsuki’s words landed a solid body blow on me, the very man who once challenged Father to a duel with Big Sister as the wager, I say. I felt as though Father were saying, “I’ll pass on someone like you too!” Ohh… Father. Whatever must I do to earn your forgiveness?
“Frankly, expecting me to take any interest in someone so high-handed is asking too much. I’d rather not be dragged around by some ability-obsessed person with no common sense.”
“Hmm… so this is the kind of reaction you get when a protagonist like Itsuki actually exists in real life. If the clichés kept piling up, romance would go completely out the window, huh…”
“I sort of understand what you mean about clichés, Naofumi-san. Rishia-san is more than enough for me.”
“Oh, speaking of Rishia-san, I hear she’s returning to school starting tomorrow.”
“Why on earth!?”
“Gaelion suggested a dream campus life with the Bow Hero, nano. If there’s bullying… the Bow Hero can fulfill his ‘executing justice’ motto, nano. Nano, nano.”
“Scattering bait like that is quite the move… no, well, perhaps it was convenient to ask her along while we’re at it…”
Oh? Itsuki doesn’t look nearly as displeased as one might expect. Secretly rather eager, it seems.
“Something the matter, nano?”

“Yes, apparently the headmaster’s side believes things should be fine, but there’s concern that residue connected to Takt or the reincarnators might still be lingering within the academy. They also apparently want to put effort into reforming the mindset of students and researchers who are trying to conduct themselves with propriety.”

Apparently this extra explanation had been given somewhere during our idle chat, or on the way here. Indeed, reincarnators have been operating in the shadows all across various regions, and while we deal with those we already know of thanks to our foreknowledge, we can’t possibly track down every distant relation among the pigs in detail, I say. There are surely pigs out there who took the tasty parts and fled, I say.

“I also think it’d be good to find students who engage in bullying and reprimand them… If someone else has to feel what I felt back in my own world, that wouldn’t be a good thing, right? I think this much justice ought to be permitted.”
“…Itsuki, you might just make a fine teacher.”
It’s likely the feeling that he doesn’t want anyone else to experience the unpleasantness he himself went through.
“Regardless of gender, anyone who engages in bullying—since I’ve been asked, I’ll make sure to catch them in the act and give them a proper reprimand.”
“In that case, having Rishia-san around really would help, wouldn’t it? She’d probably be quite useful in flushing out troublemakers.”
“Disposal of pigs, I say!”
Buzz buzz, I say! Pigs ought either be culled or shipped off to Pig King, that’s the best course, I say!
“Setting Motoyasu-kun aside… you mean like grabbing hold of a student’s tail and dealing with them, the way you just described?”
“Of course, apparently there are various things they’d also like to hear from me directly.”
“I see… well, why not? Itsuki seems motivated too, though breaking flags without savoring them isn’t all that satisfying, you know?”
“Flag Breaker, nano.”
“That’s just fine by me!”

“Flag… ah, wait, I get it! I understand now. The developing-teacher-slash-instructor storyline… taking charge of the underachievers’ class and turning the students into the academy’s best—now that’s a proper classic development!”
At Father’s words, Itsuki’s shoulders slumped, all the tension draining out of him.
“I see… so that’s a flag too, then. I’ll keep it in mind. Let’s check whether they’re dividing classes by ability or grades, and whether any oppression is occurring.”
Itsuki began to smile in a rather sinister way.
“It’s not quite Ren, but it feels like Itsuki’s chuunibyou is coming out in a different direction… I suppose it’s a good thing he can still keep it under control, at least…”
“Let’s use the hero’s authority to its fullest and take a bold scalpel to this academy’s policies… I do wonder just how far that headmaster is hoping to go… I’m rather looking forward to it.”
Itsuki does love justice, when all is said and done, I say. He could just do the Filolial mask routine with Fleon-chan instead, but no, he insists on venting it elsewhere, I say.
“As for the academy’s coliseum, the tournaments, the ranking system—if any of that exists, let’s have it abolished. Truly pointless, all of it.”
I sense something like a personal grudge lurking there, I say. Well, Itsuki apparently was an underachiever back in his own world, I say.

“There’s probably something like that, isn’t there, nano? Gaelion recalls hearing something of the sort, nano. Takt supposedly bragged about winning some martial arts tournament, nano. Heard he was also a top student in magic, nano.”

“So it’s not the theatrical-release Rafuemon storyline, but more of an academy-magic-battle development, huh? If it gets abolished, would it just turn into a straightforward practical exam? The kind where you break a target?”
“Quite a lot of flags, aren’t there… National tournaments are fine, but if there’s pointless in-school combat going on, I’ll have it abolished, heh heh heh…”
“Some other switch of Itsuki’s has flipped on… this definitely isn’t justice anymore. This is one hundred percent Itsuki’s trauma talking.”

Itsuki kept up that eerie smile for a good while afterward. According to Father, this was the venting of pent-up frustration from Itsuki’s original world, separate from the whole awakening-through-Fleon-chan’s-singing business. I too recall having countless competitions related to club activities, I say. Oddly enough there were sometimes two clubs for the very same sport, I say. Incidentally, upon investigation, it turned out there was no ranking system visible to every individual student. However, apparently there were in-school tournaments of some kind, and on Itsuki’s advice these were suspended, I say. Apparently it had been a venue for nobles to show off just how capable their own children were. What with the corruption that was already present, compounded by the fact that it had become a breeding ground for reincarnators, the school had no choice but to keep quiet about it, or so it seems.
“Naofumi, is a tournament really so bad, nano?”

“I don’t think it’s bad exactly, but once you start ranking people, you inevitably end up singling out those with lower ability. I think Itsuki’s policy is that he doesn’t want strength to be the sole criterion for evaluation. Apparently, before Rishia-san’s talent blossomed, she actually had excellent grades in writing, language, and other subjects.”
“I see, nano. The exact opposite policy of Siltvelt, nano.”
“I wonder if that’s how schools in Siltvelt tend to be? Though that place leans more toward racial factors than magical specialization, so it’s hard to say for certain…”

Siltvelt does have that aspect of “strength above all else” running through it to a considerable degree, I say. If anything, it’s a nation that built up its national power precisely by honing that principle, I say.

“I suppose what Itsuki means is that rather than making students endure that kind of bitterness at such an early stage, they should be exploring their possibilities instead? A multi-angle perspective, so to speak.”
“Heh heh… I can’t seem to stop laughing. No wait, this flow is… Naofumi-san, if I start acting strange, please stop me.”
“You’re already acting strange, so let’s stop the laughing right there. I’ll help keep you in check, but let’s rely on Rafuemon and Rishia-san too, Itsuki.”

“Understood. To start, I’ll first demonstrate my strength as a hero, then negate it by playing an instrument… spreading the message that strength isn’t everything. Surely, in the peaceful world to come, that approach will serve better.”
And so, with Father putting a stop to his laughter, Itsuki seemed to have settled firmly on his teaching policy.
After that, Itsuki was to hold a class and headed to the lecture venue as an instructor. It appeared to be the academy’s athletic field cum gymnasium, I say.
“Ahem… now then, allow me to present the Bow Hero who saved the world! Students, listen carefully and take this to heart!”
Following the teacher’s introduction, Itsuki stepped up onto the platform and surveyed the students.

“I am Itsuki Kawasumi, the Bow Hero, invited to serve as an instructor here at this magic academy for a time, at the request of various nations and the academy itself. I look forward to your acquaintance.”
Itsuki delivered a flawless greeting, I say. The students, each in their own little clusters, cast curious glances his way, I say.

“In a world different from this one… I was once a student not so different in age from all of you, but through a peculiar turn of events, I ended up coming to this world as the Bow Hero. Well, many things happened along the way—including the threat of the Waves, battles against reincarnators, the great calamity in Melromarc—and through all these various events, I find myself standing here today.”
A neat summary of everything that had happened thus far, I say.

“As for the strength you all expect of a hero in this world, I imagine it’s difficult to judge just by looking at me now. So rather than explain in words, I think it’ll be quicker to show you through action first.”
So saying, Itsuki had the gymnasium doors thrown wide open, then pointed toward the schoolyard and the sky beyond it, visible to everyone, and began chanting a spell.

『I, the Bow Hero, command the heavens, command the earth; sever the principle, bind it anew, and let the corruption be expelled. O power of the dragon vein! Combine with my magic power and the power of the hero to forge strength; the Bow Hero, the very wellspring of power, commands it. Decipher the workings of all creation once more, and summon forth a tornado to bring cataclysm!』
“Liberation Tornado!”

Aiming skyward, Itsuki unleashed the spell with a swift incantation, I say. Then the tornado he had loosed roared upward, kicking up a violent storm high into the sky, tore straight across the schoolyard, obliterated the outer wall without a trace, and went flying off far into the distance, I say.
“Th-that can’t be… the barrier, made of anti-magic-resistant material, supposedly able to withstand even ceremonial-magic-class spells…”
One of the students and a teacher muttered, at a loss for words, I say.
“I haven’t even shown my true strength yet, but is this enough to give you a sense of my capability?”
The students, teacher included, nodded at Itsuki’s question with eyes full of awe, I say.

“Now then, this time—why don’t one of you try casting a spell at me? Fast, Zweite, Drifa, whichever you like. My companions have taught me a great deal about magic, so I have a fairly thorough grasp of it.”
At Itsuki’s words, the teacher raised a hand and chanted a spell in his direction, I say. Itsuki instantly nullified it using techniques drawn from the Way of the Dragon Vein, halting its activation.
“No way… They say it’s theoretically possible, but to nullify even a Drifa-class spell… just how…”
The teacher muttered in astonishment, pondering possible countermeasures, I say.

“I likely couldn’t block ceremonial magic on my own. Let’s leave the preamble at that. Indeed, when it comes to combat magic, this much is within my ability. But if we’re talking about heroes, most of the other heroes besides myself can manage about this much as well.”
By “most,” I suppose he meant to set Father apart, since Father is unable to use offensive magic, I say.
“It’s true that as a hero, I’m likely far stronger than any of you when it comes to combat ability. But is the magic you’re all studying here at this academy limited only to offensive spells?”
At Itsuki’s question, the students exchanged glances and began murmuring amongst their groups, I say.
“Of course, I too understand that magic isn’t solely about combat application. But when it comes to that kind of applied knowledge, I’m sure my knowledge and experience fall short of yours.”

“That’s the old ‘lower them then raise them up’ trick, I bet,” Father murmured to Rival and me while cloaked in stealth, I say. Rival, seeming to understand that much herself, nodded, I say. Naturally, so did I, I say.

“Strength isn’t everything. What matters to me is what remains once that strength is no longer used. As for my own innate talent, I only truly became aware of it after coming to this world. The talent I originally possessed had… limits, and it was the kind evaluated as low-ability.”

Itsuki swiftly produced an instrument and began to play. It was the very melody that the Filolial-samas and Elephant sing, I say. And yet the tune Itsuki drew from it carried a weight rivaling that of the Filolial-sama’s own song—so profound in tone that even the surrounding students found themselves drawn in, listening intently. Well, Itsuki had, after all, played instruments alongside Filolial-samas other than Fleon-chan at mealtime gatherings back in the village, livening up the atmosphere, I say.
